# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 3 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** The Righteous and the Sinner

---

**3:1** Why do you slumber, O my soul,
and not bless the LORD?

**3:2** Sing a new song to God who is worthy of praise;
sing and be glad of heart, all you who honor him.

**3:3** The LORD instructs the righteous through discipline;
the life of the righteous is in the instruction of the LORD.

**3:4** Our God is compassionate and merciful;
he forgives and he saves.

**3:5** The righteous stumbles, and the LORD vindicates him;
he falls, and watches to see what God will do for him.

**3:6** He looks for where his help will come from
and fixes his eyes on God.

**3:7** The righteous man does not spare himself
when he makes atonement for an unwitting sin;

**3:8** he cleanses his soul from defilement
and looks to the LORD for pardon from the sin of ignorance,

**3:9** that it not be counted against him as a deliberate sin,
nor that an enemy trample over him.

**3:10** The sinner stumbles and curses his own life,
the day when he was born and his mother's labor.

**3:11** He heaps sin upon sin in his life;
he falls — a grievous fall — and he shall not rise.

**3:12** The destruction of the sinner is forever;
he shall not be remembered when God visits the righteous.
This is the lot of sinners forever.
But those who fear the LORD shall rise to eternal life,
and their life shall be in the light of the LORD, and shall not fail.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering integrating EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA. Preferred readings noted where agents diverge.*
